newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares surge to new high, led by Ericsson.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares surge to new high, led by Ericsson.

text.p: Swedish shares closed at a high on Wednesday for the third consecutive day with the mood in the market upbeat and market heavyweight Ericsson heading the climb with a 5.3 percent jump.
The general index rose 1.25 percent to 2,980.57. Shares totalling 6.43 billion crowns changed owners.
Market heavyweight Ericsson surged 15.5 crowns to 307.5. Brokers attributed the rise to SmithBarney setting a $59 price for Ericsson shares on top of a buy recommendation.
"The whole telecommunications sector is strong. The recommendation was just in time," one broker said.

Drugs major Astra rose two to 143 crowns. The FDA approved its asthma treatment Pulmicort Turbuhaler for the U.S. late on Tuesday. Brokers said the approval, which had been expected for a couple of weeks, was already discounted.
Vehicle maker Volvo ended three crowns higher at 200.5 after saying it had sold its entire stake in Scandinavian airline SAS for a capital gain of 221 million crowns. SAS rose one crown to 93.
Bar code reading systems maker Pricer rose 10 crowns to 278 after completing a share issue to institutional investors to finance the purchase of U.S. Intactix.
Lehman Brothers was the largest net buyer of shares, scooping up shares totalling 9.4 million crowns of a total turnover of 19.7 million crowns.
